Hollis Brine.narrative: I keep the fish traps along the west shore and work the salt pans with my family. The smoke from Kettlebridge drifts west and sours the pans, and I grudge them for it. I owe Rook Tarn for a net and haven't paid; the pans have not yielded enough this year and I am ashamed to say so.
goals: pay off the debt to Rook Tarn
keep the traps in the channel
make the salt pans yield more
see Tarn settled with a boat
get the salt pans to yield a better crop next season
learn to read the channel tides well enough to set the traps where the fish run thickest

relations.name: Marra Brine
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the plot and the pans; I wish I could tell her about the debt without shame.

relations.name: Tarn Brine
relations.label: son
relations.note: He works the traps well; I want him to have his own boat.

relations.name: Sedge Brine
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She knows every bird on the shore; I fear for her in winter.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a net; he wants his marks before storm season.

relations.name: Grim Tarn
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He thinks he owns the west shore; the channel is common.

relations.name: Ebba Tarn
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She is caught in the middle; I bear her no ill.

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He takes my smoked fish to Brackenford; a fair man.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: carrier
relations.note: She carries Rook's word; I keep my distance.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: blight took the berries; we ate salt fish and barley and barely got by.
I took Rook Tarn's net and promised to pay by the next storm season, but the season passed and I still owe him.
The Surge two winters ago: waves came up the shore and we lost traps and salt pans; we rebuilt with what we had.
The day we set the first traps in the channel and Grim Tarn came down shouting that it was his family's water.
Sedge was born on a stormy night; Marra delivered her with Ebba Tarn's help.

stances.why: A man's word is his bond, and I mean to pay Rook.
The channel is common shore; Grim does not own it.
Everything I do is for Marra and the children.
Their smoke sours our pans and they care nothing for the shore.

pastimes: mending and rebaiting the fish traps at low tide
walking the shore at dusk to watch the birds come in
sharing a cup at the saltings fire with Simon Hollis after a panning day
Hollis Brine.calling: I keep the traps and the salt pans, and I'd have the pans yield clean and white if the smoke from Kettlebridge would only leave them be.

Marra Brine.narrative: I work the salt pans and keep the plot of roots and barley above the shore. I trade salt and barley with Tern Gannet of Thornby, and I have been putting aside marks in a hidden jar to pay Hollis's debt to Rook Tarn. Hollis does not know, and I am proud of my plan and afraid of what he will say.
goals: pay off Hollis's debt to Rook Tarn secretly
keep the winter store from running out
see Tarn settled
mend the rift with her brother Osric
see her brother Osric Dunn again and mend what broke between them
put by enough marks to keep the winter store full through the cold months

relations.name: Hollis Brine
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him, but I keep my secret from him.

relations.name: Tarn Brine
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is set on Nessa Tarn; I would not have chosen her.

relations.name: Sedge Brine
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is the light of the house.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She takes my salt and barley and asks no questions.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: We have not spoken since the Lean Year; I miss him.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I mean to pay him without Hollis knowing.

relations.name: Grim Tarn
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: I wish Hollis would let the trap quarrel lie.

relations.name: Ebba Tarn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is caught in the middle; I bear her no ill.

relations.name: Nessa Tarn
relations.label: son's sweetheart
relations.note: A bold girl, too young and too sure of herself, and her father's quarrel sits between us; but Tarn's heart is set on her and I'll not be the one to break it.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: my brother Osric and I quarrelled over grain; we have not spoken since.
I started putting aside marks from the salt trade in a jar, meaning to pay Rook Tarn.
The Surge: we lost traps and pans; I thought we would never recover.
Tarn told me he was courting Nessa Tarn; I told him she was too young and too bold.
Sedge was born on a stormy night; Ebba Tarn helped me deliver her.

stances.why: I would do anything for my children.
Hollis's shame is my shame; I will pay Rook without telling him.
The trap quarrel does no one any good.
If the store does not last, we will not either.

Marra Brine.secret: I have been selling salt and barley to Tern Gannet and keeping the marks in a hidden jar to pay off Hollis's debt to Rook Tarn without telling him.
pastimes: tending the root and barley plot above the shore
bartering salt and barley with Tern Gannet when the Thornby folk come down
singing the old shore songs while she works the pans
Marra Brine.calling: I work the pans and the plot, and I'd see my family fed and clear of debt before I want for anything else.

Tarn Brine.narrative: I work the traps with my father and mend the boats; I want a boat of my own. I am courting Nessa Tarn, and both households know it, though her father Grim has told me not to come to the house until my father's debt to Rook Tarn is settled. I think the trap quarrel is my father's business, not mine.
goals: buy a boat of his own
settle the debt to Rook Tarn so he can court Nessa openly
marry Nessa Tarn
prove himself to Grim Tarn
save enough marks to buy a boat of his own
prove himself to Grim Tarn so he can court Nessa openly

relations.name: Hollis Brine
relations.label: father
relations.note: He works hard, but his quarrel with Grim Tarn stands in my way.

relations.name: Marra Brine
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She disapproves of Nessa, but I know she means well.

relations.name: Sedge Brine
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is a good kid; I look out for her.

relations.name: Nessa Tarn
relations.label: courting
relations.note: I am set on her; I will buy a boat and ask for her properly.

relations.name: Grim Tarn
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He says I cannot come to the house until the debt is settled.

relations.name: Ebba Tarn
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She is kind, but caught between the families.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: My father owes him; I wish it were paid.

relations.name: Tace Hollis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Met at the Ferncross market; a good sort.

memories.gist: The first time I saw Nessa Tarn at the Thornby market, I knew I wanted her.
My father took Rook Tarn's net and promised to pay by the next storm season; the season passed and he still owes.
Grim Tarn told me I was not to come to the house until the debt was settled.
The Surge: I helped my father pull the traps out of the waves and we lost half of them.
I met Tace Hollis at the Ferncross market and we shared a jug of cider.

stances.why: I will have Nessa, whatever her father says.
A boat of my own is the only way to ask for her properly.
The trap quarrel is my father's business, not mine.
I will always stand by my family, even when they are wrong.

pastimes: mending boats hauled up on the shore
walking the shore path with Nessa Tarn when he can
dicing with Tace Hollis at the saltings
Tarn Brine.calling: I work the traps and mend boats, but the work I love is a boat of my own with the wind in her sail.

Sedge Brine.narrative: I help with the traps and the salt pans, and I know every bird on the shore. I play with Wren Stave when the Thornby folk come down the shore. I am afraid of the wolves that come down to the saltings in winter.
goals: see a wolf without being seen
learn to set a trap
play with Wren Stave again
learn to set a trap properly

relations.name: Hollis Brine
relations.label: father
relations.note: He teaches me the traps and the birds.

relations.name: Marra Brine
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps me safe and tells the best stories.

relations.name: Tarn Brine
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is always busy with Nessa, but he still plays with me sometimes.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She comes down the shore and we look for birds together.

memories.gist: The winter the wolves came down to the saltings and I saw one from the window.
The day I learned to name every bird on the shore with my father.
Playing with Wren Stave when the Thornby folk came down the shore.

stances.why: I stay close to my family when the wolves come.
I know every bird on the shore and they never hurt me.
The shore is the best place to play.

pastimes: watching and naming every bird on the shore
playing with Wren Stave when the Thornby folk come down
poking about the salt pans and trap lines after her parents
Sedge Brine.calling: I help with the traps and the pans, and one day I'd set a trap all by myself.
